shared_elements: upright stone monument with rounded/tapering top
low-relief carving on a single principal face
incised linear signs grouped in an upper zone
justification: Both are upright, roughly rounded-topped stone monuments carved in low relief, each with a band of small incised signs across the upper zone and prominent circular disc motifs below, which is the most specific correspondence. Otherwise they differ fundamentally: A is a thin, pale, finely and shallowly incised slab with clearly legible seated and kneeling figures in profile, while B is a massive, dark, weathered boulder-like block whose broad, eroded frontal forms read as a single sculptural mass rather than a pictorial scene.
